title: Clause-level versioned-revision benchmark with version-selection metrics and cross-retriever arms
description: Build and release a clause-level benchmark of overlapping successive revisions from an amended regulatory corpus: archived version snapshots, per-clause effective and expiry dates, time-stamped queries with target dates, gold in-force version labels per query, and published retrieval-layer metrics (version-selection accuracy@k, Recall@k, MRR, nDCG@k) alongside end-answer accuracy. Include arms using BM25 and at least two dense encoders under matched segmentation and top-k to test the retrieval-agnosticism claim.
why_differs: Prior et al.'s benchmark is evaluated only through LLM-judged end answers with no retrieval metrics and no per-passage version labels, TIQ tests temporal reasoning over non-versioned snippets, and TempRALM evaluates gold-passage recall on Wikipedia rather than regulatory amendments.
technical_mechanism: Corpus construction pipeline that snapshots statute versions, aligns clauses across amendments, records effective/expiry dates, and derives per-passage version labels used to compute version-selection accuracy at query target dates.
expected_benefit: Supplies the missing measurement instrument for the whole line of work, makes version-selection accuracy comparable across methods, and allows the retrieval-agnosticism claim to be tested rather than asserted.
potential_novelty: Hedged: no retrieved resource provides clause-level overlapping revisions with in-force labels and retrieval metrics, but this is a bounded negative finding since the search budget was exhausted and some venues were unreachable.
implementation_difficulty_basis: Amended statute corpora are large and versioning metadata is often incomplete; clause-level alignment across versions and effective/expiry dates must be reconstructed, and exact reproduction requires archiving snapshots because legislation changes.
experimental_difficulty_basis: Requires curating version history and validity intervals, query construction with expert checking, and cross-retriever runs; the effort is dominated by data curation and annotation rather than compute.
main_risk: High curation cost with construct-validity risk: if queries are synthesised by an LLM, measured gains may not transfer to real legal queries, and a small benchmark limits statistical power for per-regime analysis.
